page: Vultr vc2-24c-96gb is a high-capacity tier within the Vultr Cloud Compute line, operating on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine provides 24 shared vCPUs derived from 12 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, supporting hyper-threading at 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is allocated at 96 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Storage is provisioned directly via 1600 GB of local NVMe SSD space, while standard connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Acceleration hardware such as GPUs is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that the server centers around moderate multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread capabilities. Synthetic processing assessments reflect this profile, with a Geekbench single-core score of 838.0 and a multi-core score of 7313.0, corroborated by stress-ng results of 1451.3 on single-core and 32078.94 on multi-core execution. PassMark CPU tests achieve 29089.76 points, supported by hardware AVX, AVX-512F, and AES cryptographic instructions. In data-handling tests, the host achieves 31.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 15.77 GB/sec static web serving throughput. However, workloads constrained by single-thread latency, such as Geekbench text processing (588.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (23.37 GB/sec), perform in lower benchmark percentiles.

From an efficiency standpoint, the vc2-24c-96gb leverages shared-core virtualization to offer large memory and storage capacities at a cost profile lower than dedicated bare-metal or compute-intensive alternatives. This architecture trades absolute single-thread determinism for dense thread availability and substantial local NVMe disk volume. As a result, the instance represents a suitable deployment option for parallel compilation jobs, batch ETL transformations, medium-scale relational databases, caching tiers, and general-purpose backend services requiring high disk capacity and memory headroom.
